need: protect the salary spreadsheets on a shared file server

only the four members of the payroll team need these files
the files must stay on the existing server

appliesWhen: users have more access to a resource than their job needs and the permissions must be limited

appliesWhen: only a known, small set of approved programs may run and everything else must be denied by default
explanation: An application allow list names the programs that are permitted to run; everything not on the list is blocked. It suits systems with a fixed purpose, because new or unknown software, including malware, cannot run.

explanation: A canary account is a decoy user account, often made to look privileged, that no real person or service uses. Because it should never be used, any authentication attempt with it is a strong sign that an attacker has found and is trying the credentials.

answer.item: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)

appliesWhen: the domain owner must set a policy (none, quarantine, or reject) for mail that fails authentication and receive reports

analysts need a record of process and file activity on each device
a compromised device must be cut off from the network from a central console

answer.item: Endpoint detection and response (EDR)

appliesWhen: endpoints need behavior-based detection, activity recording, and the ability to isolate a device and respond
explanation: EDR continuously collects activity from endpoints, uses behavior and signature analysis to find suspicious actions, and alerts analysts. It lets them investigate and respond, for example by isolating an endpoint or stopping a process.

appliesWhen: traffic must be allowed or blocked by addresses, protocols, and ports, with everything not explicitly allowed denied
explanation: A rule-based firewall checks each packet against an ordered list of rules (an access control list) that names source, destination, protocol, and port. A rule allows only the needed traffic, and the final implicit deny blocks everything else.

appliesWhen: a system still has default settings, unused services, or default credentials that add to its attack surface
explanation: Hardening reduces a system's attack surface: it removes software and services that are not needed, disables unused ports and protocols, changes default passwords, and applies a secure baseline. Each service that is removed is one less way in for an attacker.

appliesWhen: one host must be protected by software on it that sees decrypted traffic and system activity and can block attacks

need: find out quickly when staff passwords leak in breaches of other sites
clues: a list from a breached shopping site held several staff email addresses with passwords
some staff use the same password at work and at home
the policy no longer forces regular password changes unless there is evidence of compromise

answer.item: Compromised credential monitoring against breached password lists

appliesWhen: the team must learn when credentials appear in known breaches and force a change
explanation: Compromised credential monitoring checks passwords against lists of breached credentials and alerts when one matches. NIST guidance says to change a password when there is evidence of compromise rather than on a fixed schedule.

need: set how files are shared in a small design studio
clues: each designer creates files and decides who else may open or edit them
a designer wants to give one colleague edit rights and the client read-only rights
there is no central classification of the files

answer.item: Discretionary access control

appliesWhen: the owner of each object decides who may access it
explanation: Discretionary access control (DAC) lets the owner of a file set its access control list, giving read, write, or other rights to each user. It is flexible but depends on owners making good choices.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: handle the account of a sales manager who left the company today
clues: the manager must not be able to sign in again from home
the replacement will need to read the manager's old email and files next month
the manager has already returned the laptop and smart card

answer.item: Disable the account and reset its password

appliesWhen: a person has left and their access must stop while the account data is kept
explanation: Deprovisioning disables the account and resets its password so the former owner cannot use it. The account is not deleted at once, because the company may still need its email and files.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: keep a way to administer the cloud identity service if normal sign-in fails
clues: every administrator signs in through the company's MFA service and federation server
an outage of that MFA service last year locked out all of the administrators
the account must not be used for daily work and every use must raise an alert

answer.item: A break-glass emergency access account kept in a safe and monitored

appliesWhen: administrators must still get in when the normal sign-in path is broken
explanation: An emergency access (break-glass) account is a highly privileged account kept for when normal administrator sign-in is unavailable, for example during an identity provider or MFA outage. Its credentials are stored securely, it does not depend on the systems that might fail, and every sign-in is monitored and raises an alert.

need: let staff from a partner company use the joint project portal
clues: the two companies do not want to merge their directories
partner staff should sign in with the accounts their own company manages
when a partner employee leaves, the partner disables the account on its side only

answer.item: Federation with the partner's identity provider

appliesWhen: users of another organization must be trusted with credentials that their own organization manages
explanation: Federation shares identity information between organizations: the partner's identity provider authenticates its own users, and the service provider trusts that result. Each company keeps managing its own accounts.

need: give forty new claims processors access to the claims share and printer
clues: each processor needs exactly the same access as the others
rights given to each user one by one have drifted apart over the years
staff join and leave the claims department every month

answer.item: Add the users to a department group that holds the permissions

appliesWhen: many users with the same job need the same permissions and must be easy to add and remove
explanation: Group-based permissions are assigned once to a group, and every member inherits them. Adding or removing a member changes that person's access without editing each resource.

need: add a second factor for the finance team's payment system
clues: finance staff were targeted by phishing pages that also captured codes they typed
the factor must be a physical device that the user carries
the company will pay for one device per user

answer.item: A hardware security key based on FIDO2

appliesWhen: a phishing-resistant factor in the form of a physical device is needed
explanation: A hardware security key is a hard token: the user must have the physical device, and it signs a cryptographic challenge for the real site. It resists phishing because there is no code that a fake page can capture and replay.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: create accounts for new employees who are hired and start work remotely
clues: no one at the company has met the new hires in person
an attacker once got an account by pretending to be a new hire on the phone
the account must be tied to the real person before any access is given

answer.item: Identity proofing that checks government-issued ID before the account is created

appliesWhen: a person's real identity must be confirmed before credentials are issued
explanation: Identity proofing verifies that a person is who they claim to be, for example with a passport or driving license, before the account is issued. It is the first step of the identity lifecycle and stops fraudulent enrollment.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: reduce the standing administrator rights on the database servers
clues: database administrators hold full admin rights all day but use them for under an hour
a stolen admin account would have full rights at any moment
admins should ask for rights through the PAM system when a task starts

answer.item: Just-in-time privileged access that expires after the task

appliesWhen: elevated rights should exist only for the time a task needs them
explanation: Just-in-time (JIT) access grants elevated permissions through the privileged access management system only when they are requested and approved, for a set time. The rights are then revoked automatically, so there are no standing privileges to steal.

need: connect an on-premises application to the company directory for sign-in
clues: the application must look up users and their group memberships
all accounts are stored as objects in the existing Active Directory
the queries must be encrypted on the network

answer.item: Secure LDAP (LDAPS) queries to the directory

appliesWhen: an application must query and authenticate against a directory service
explanation: LDAP is the protocol that reads and changes directory service data such as users, groups, and computers in Active Directory. LDAPS runs it over TLS so the queries and credentials are encrypted.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: let lab technicians install software on the computers in the science labs
clues: the technicians are currently members of the domain admins group
they never need to change servers, the directory, or other departments' computers
their rights should end at the lab computers

answer.item: Grant administrator rights only on the lab computers through a local administrator group

appliesWhen: a person needs admin rights on a few machines but not across the whole domain
explanation: A global privileged account such as a domain admin has rights on every system, while a local privileged account has rights on one machine only. Least privilege gives the technicians local rights on the lab computers and nothing more.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: control access to intelligence reports
clues: every report is labeled Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential
each analyst has a clearance level from a background check
the authors of the reports must not be able to share them with anyone they choose

answer.item: Mandatory access control

appliesWhen: access is decided by comparing data classification labels with user clearances
explanation: Mandatory access control (MAC) compares the classification label of the data with the clearance of the user, and the system enforces the decision. Owners cannot change who has access.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: let a new scheduling app read users' calendars in the cloud mail service
clues: the app must never see or store the users' mail passwords
each user should approve what the app may access
the access should be limited in scope and time and be easy to revoke

answer.item: OAuth tokens issued by the authorization server

appliesWhen: a third-party application needs delegated access to a user's resources without the password
explanation: OAuth is a framework for delegated authorization: the user approves access, and the authorization server gives the app a token with a set scope and duration. The app uses the token instead of the user's credentials.

need: confirm the identity of online shoppers before large card purchases
clues: the shoppers are customers, not employees, and will not install an app
almost all customers have a registered mobile phone number
the code should be valid only for a short time and work only once

answer.item: A one-time password sent to the customer's phone

appliesWhen: a short-lived code must reach users who have no app or hardware device
explanation: A one-time password (OTP) is a short-lived code that works once, for example a code sent to the user's phone during a purchase. It adds a second factor for users who have no authenticator app or token.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 19: Given a scenario, implement and maintain identity and access management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management

need: replace passwords for customers who sign in to the online store
clues: customers keep falling for fake login pages that steal their passwords
customers want to sign in with the fingerprint or face unlock of their phone
the sign-in secret must be tied to the real web site and sync between the customer's devices

answer.item: Passkeys based on the FIDO standards

appliesWhen: a phishing-resistant, passwordless sign-in that works with the user's own device unlock is needed
explanation: A passkey is a FIDO credential made of a key pair: the private key stays on the user's devices and is unlocked with a biometric or PIN, and the site keeps only the public key. It is bound to the real site, so a fake page cannot use it.

need: show the auditors that the password policy is applied to every account
clues: some old accounts were created before the current policy
the auditors ask for a list of accounts whose passwords never expire or are blank
nobody knows how many dormant accounts still have passwords

answer.item: An account audit with a password policy report

appliesWhen: the team must prove which accounts do and do not meet the password policy
explanation: Account auditing reviews accounts against the password policy, and a policy report lists the accounts that do not comply, such as passwords that never expire. It finds weak or dormant accounts that the policy settings alone do not reveal.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 19: Implementing and Maintaining Identity and Access Management; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 23: Summarizing Elements of Effective Security Governance

need: stop users from going back to their old password after a forced change
clues: users change their password several times in a row to get back to the old one
the old password appeared in an earlier incident
the system remembers no earlier passwords

answer.item: Password history combined with a minimum password age

appliesWhen: users must not reuse old passwords or cycle quickly back to them
explanation: Password history (reuse) blocks the last several passwords, and a minimum password age stops users from changing the password many times in a row to cycle back. Together they stop reuse of an old, possibly exposed password.

need: update the password policy for staff accounts
clues: users choose short passwords such as Spring24! to meet the complexity rule
a cracking test broke most eight-character passwords in hours
users find long phrases of several words easy to remember

answer.item: A minimum length of 15 characters with passphrases allowed

appliesWhen: passwords are cracked because they are too short
explanation: Length adds the most strength to a password because each extra character multiplies the number of possible combinations. Current NIST guidance favors long passphrases over short complex passwords.

need: help staff who use dozens of web services that each need a password
clues: many staff use the same password for every service
others write their passwords on notes stuck to the monitor
each service should get a long random password that no one needs to remember

answer.item: A company-approved password manager

appliesWhen: users must keep many unique strong passwords without remembering them
explanation: A password manager stores passwords in an encrypted vault, generates a strong unique password for each account, and fills it in. The user only has to remember one strong master password.

need: set access in the loan system for 300 staff in a few job functions
clues: every loan officer needs the same set of operations, and so does every underwriter
staff move between jobs often
access should follow the job a person does, not the person

answer.item: Role-based access control

appliesWhen: access is given by job function through sets of permissions
explanation: Role-based access control (RBAC) groups permissions into roles that match job functions, and users get access by being assigned a role. When a person changes jobs, a new role replaces the old one.

need: control which connections can reach the management interface of the network devices
clues: access must be allowed only from the IT subnet
the same conditions apply to every user, whatever their job
an administrator sets the conditions centrally, not the owners of each device

answer.item: Rule-based access control

appliesWhen: the same system-wide conditions, such as source address, decide access for everyone
explanation: Rule-based access control applies rules set by an administrator, such as allowed IP addresses, to every access request. The rules apply to all users, unlike roles that depend on the job.

need: let staff sign in once and then open several web-based business applications
clues: the company's identity provider already authenticates every user
the web applications accept XML assertions about the user from a trusted provider
users currently have a different password for each application

answer.item: SAML-based single sign-on

appliesWhen: web applications must accept a signed XML assertion from the company's identity provider for single sign-on
explanation: SAML is an XML-based standard in which the identity provider sends a signed assertion about the user to the service provider. It lets users sign in once and reach many web applications without storing passwords in each one.

need: reduce the risk from how the domain administrators use their accounts
clues: the administrators read email and browse the web while signed in with full domain rights
a phishing link opened by one of them would run with the highest privileges
the administrators need high privileges only for a few tasks each day

answer.item: Give each administrator a standard user account and a separate privileged account

appliesWhen: people with admin duties use one powerful account for everyday work
explanation: Privileged users should have two accounts: a standard user account for email and browsing, and a privileged account only for admin tasks. Malware that runs in the everyday session then does not get admin rights.

need: fix how the nightly backup software signs in to the file servers
clues: the backup jobs run under the personal account of one systems administrator
the jobs failed the night the administrator changed his password
the software only needs to read the file shares and write to the backup storage

answer.item: Create a dedicated service account with only the rights the backup needs

appliesWhen: an application or scheduled job needs its own non-human identity
explanation: A service account is a non-interactive account that an application or service runs under. It should have only the rights the service needs and be monitored closely, so the job does not depend on a person's account.

need: add a second factor for all staff when they sign in to cloud email
clues: every employee already has a company smartphone
there is no budget to buy and ship physical devices
codes must work even when the phone has no mobile signal

answer.item: An authenticator app that generates time-based codes

appliesWhen: a second factor is needed on devices users already carry, without buying hardware
explanation: A soft token is software, such as an authenticator app, that generates time-based one-time codes on the user's phone. It needs no extra hardware, and the codes are generated on the device without a network connection.

need: make sure every workstation locks an account after five wrong passwords
clues: the rule must apply to all 2,000 domain computers at once
the rule must not depend on users remembering or agreeing to it
the systems should enforce it the same way every time

answer.item: A technical policy enforced through the directory's group policy

appliesWhen: a rule must be enforced automatically by systems rather than by people
explanation: Logical or technical access policies are enforced by the systems themselves, for example account lockout pushed by group policy. They apply consistently and cannot be ignored by users.

need: give the support engineers of the lab system's vendor remote access
clues: the vendor's engineers currently share the login of an employee who has left
nobody can tell which engineer made which change on the lab system
the vendor needs access only while a support case is open

answer.item: Create individual third-party accounts that are limited to the system and expire

appliesWhen: people from an outside company need their own controlled access to company systems
explanation: Third-party accounts give outside people such as vendors and contractors their own identities with limited rights and an end date. Individual accounts make their actions traceable, and the limits keep a vendor compromise from reaching other systems.

need: stop cleaning contractors from signing in to the reception PCs at night
clues: the contractors need the PCs only from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. on weekdays
the security team saw sign-ins on these accounts at two in the morning
the hours should be enforced by the system

answer.item: Time-based access control

appliesWhen: access must be limited to set hours or days
explanation: Time-based access control, such as time-of-day restrictions, allows sign-in only during set hours. It removes the off-hours window that an attacker or insider could use.

need: handle low-risk phishing reports without an analyst doing every step

it should plan and carry out several steps toward a goal with little human input
its actions must stay inside limits that the team sets and be logged

answer.item: Agentic AI that acts within set guardrails

appliesWhen: an AI system must plan and carry out multistep tasks on its own toward a goal
explanation: Agentic AI can plan and carry out several steps toward a goal and take actions with tools, not just answer questions. Because it acts on its own, it needs guardrails, limited permissions, and logging.

need: spot account misuse that fixed alert thresholds miss
clues: each user and server has its own normal pattern of activity
fixed thresholds raise many false alarms for some users and miss others
the normal pattern should update itself as work habits change

answer.item: AI-augmented baselines of normal user and entity behavior

appliesWhen: a learned, changing model of normal behavior is needed for each user or system
explanation: AI-augmented baselines use machine learning to learn the normal behavior of each user and system and keep updating it. Activity that differs from that baseline is flagged, which finds misuse that fixed thresholds miss.

need: answer the many staff questions about security policy and how to report phishing
clues: the help desk gets hundreds of the same questions each week
staff want answers in plain language at any hour
the tool only needs to talk with users, not change any systems

answer.item: An AI chatbot trained on the security policies

appliesWhen: users need conversational answers to common questions at any time
explanation: An AI chatbot holds a conversation in natural language and answers common questions at any time of day. It reduces help desk load by handling routine requests, so staff can focus on harder issues.
source: IBM Think – What is a chatbot?; AWS – What is a chatbot?

need: decide which systems to patch and monitor first next quarter
clues: years of incident, vulnerability, and outage data are stored in the SIEM
the team wants to forecast where problems are most likely to happen
the aim is to act before an incident rather than after it

answer.item: AI predictive analysis of historical security data

appliesWhen: historical data must be used to forecast likely future events so the team can act early
explanation: Predictive analysis uses statistical models and machine learning on historical data to forecast likely future events, such as which systems are most likely to fail or be attacked. It makes security work more proactive.

need: find unusual activity in millions of log lines each day
clues: two analysts read the logs by hand and fall days behind
an attacker's off-hours logins last year were seen only weeks later
the team wants an alert as soon as activity differs from the usual pattern

answer.item: Automated anomaly detection that analyzes logs and raises alerts

appliesWhen: large volumes of events must be checked continuously for activity that differs from normal
explanation: Automated anomaly detection analyzes logs in real time and alerts when activity differs from the normal pattern. It finds threats faster than manual review and frees analysts for the investigation.

need: find security flaws in code changes before they reach production

security testing now happens by hand once a quarter
a SQL injection flaw reached the live site before anyone tested it

explanation: Continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) builds and tests each code change automatically, including static analysis and security tests, before deployment. Flaws are found early, when they are cheaper to fix.

need: decide whether to buy an automation platform for log analysis
clues: the platform costs $40,000 up front and $10,000 a year
two analysts spend much of their time on log review today
the board wants to know whether the platform will pay for itself

answer.item: A cost-benefit analysis of the automation

appliesWhen: the financial costs of automation must be weighed against its expected savings
explanation: Automation has up-front and ongoing costs for software, hardware, and staff. A cost-benefit analysis compares them with the expected savings, such as analyst time, before the company commits.

need: keep the configuration of 400 servers in line with the security baseline
clues: admins sometimes change settings by hand during an outage and never change them back
a disabled audit setting was found on several servers months later
the baseline is already written as configuration files

answer.item: Desired state management that checks and corrects the configuration

appliesWhen: systems drift from a defined configuration and must be returned to it automatically
explanation: Desired state management declares how each system should be configured, then checks the systems and corrects any drift automatically. It enforces the baseline continuously instead of only at build time.

answer.item: Converting all timestamps to one time zone such as UTC

appliesWhen: logs from several time zones must be put in one correct order
explanation: Time normalization converts timestamps from different time zones into one common zone, such as UTC or GMT. Only then can events from several systems be placed in a true chronological sequence.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 21: Explain appropriate incident response activities

need: preserve the state of a compromised virtual machine in the company's private cloud
clues: the hypervisor can save the VM's disk and memory state at one point in time
the business wants the evidence captured in seconds without touching the guest operating system
the VM must later be rebuilt from a clean template

answer.item: A snapshot of the virtual machine

appliesWhen: the system is a virtual machine and its state must be captured quickly from the hypervisor
explanation: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of a virtual machine's state that the hypervisor takes without logging in to the guest. It preserves the compromised VM for later analysis before the VM is rebuilt.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 21: Understanding Appropriate Incident Response Activities; CompTIA Security+ Practice Tests: Exam SY0-701 (Seidl) – Chapter 4: Domain 4.0: Security Operations

need: find out what changed on a file server that was compromised last week
clues: monthly scan reports for the server are kept for two years
the team suspects that a new service and an extra open port appeared before the attack
the reports list open ports, installed software, and known weaknesses

answer.item: A comparison of the server's historical vulnerability scan reports

appliesWhen: the team must see how a system's open ports, software, or known weaknesses changed over time
explanation: Vulnerability scans record open ports, services, software, and weaknesses at a point in time. Comparing an older scan with a recent one shows changes, such as new open ports or unauthorized software, that may explain an incident.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Cert Guide (Heuermann) – Chapter 22: Using Data Sources to Support an Investigation; CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 22: Given a scenario, use data sources to support an investigation

need: find out who has been probing the public website for hidden admin pages
clues: the team needs each visitor's source address, the pages requested, and the status codes returned
thousands of requests for pages that do not exist arrived in one hour
the site is static content, so no application on it records user actions

answer.item: The web server logs

appliesWhen: the question is which addresses connected to a web server, which pages they asked for, and what status codes it returned
explanation: Web server logs record every connection to the server with the source address, the page or resource requested, and the status code. Many requests that return errors from one address point to scanning for hidden pages.
source: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 Certification Guide, 3rd edition (Neil) – Chapter 22: Given a scenario, use data sources to support an investigation
